key_insight: A more rigorous Polish medical exam benchmark revealed that top LLM performance can drop sharply when MCQA shortcuts and answer biases are reduced, suggesting prior scores may overstate true competence.
clinical_relevance: For medical AI evaluation, this means exam-style accuracy alone may not be a reliable proxy for real clinical reasoning or readiness.
method: Expanded Polish medical exam benchmark by adding 15,000+ questions
Added two new domains and four structural changes to reduce MCQA artifacts
Evaluated 21 LLMs on English and Polish versions of the exams
evidence_signal: The hardest setup caused the best model, Qwen3.5-122B, to fall by 28.4 points on English and 31 points on Polish exams, despite low evidence of data contamination.
watch_item: Even with improved benchmarking, exam performance may still miss real-world clinical judgment, so results should not be interpreted as direct evidence of clinical safety or competence.
paper_title: Reassessing High-Performing LLMs on Polish Medical Exams: True Competence or Bias-Driven Performance?
